slides.title: A 10-minute logo sketch could sell for $20K
slides.sub: The pencil drawing behind MrBeast's logo goes to auction this week. Here's what it says about the logo your business runs on.

slides.title: The auction estimate
slides.body: Heritage Auctions puts the original 2018 pencil sketch of MrBeast's big cat logo at around $20,000. Online bidding runs October 23 to 25.

slides.title: It took about ten minutes
slides.body: He told the design team he liked big jungle cats. The artist sketched one, and he approved it on the spot, per Heritage Auctions.

slides.title: It started with a generic image
slides.body: Before the sketch, MrBeast used a generic image he found online as his logo. He was advised to create something unique to his channel.

slides.title: Time is not the value
slides.body: That sketch matters because of years of consistent use. A logo earns its value every time a customer sees it and knows it's you.

slides.title: Ownership is the real asset
slides.body: The buyer takes home paper. The rights to the logo stay with the brand, and that is where a logo's real value lives.

caption:
MrBeast logo sketch auction checklist: 4 things Black-owned businesses should check on their own logo.

Heritage Auctions is selling the original 2018 pencil sketch of MrBeast's big cat logo, with an estimate of around $20,000. Online bidding runs October 23 to 25. The sketch took about ten minutes to draw. Before it, MrBeast used a generic image he found online. The buyer gets the paper only, with no rights to the logo.

Here's what to check on your own logo:
1. It is original, never a template or an image pulled from the internet.
2. You own the files and the rights, in writing.
3. It still reads at profile-picture size.
4. You use it the same way everywhere, every time.

A logo earns its value through years of consistent use. Start with one that is truly yours.
